title: Slashy vs Notion Mail: Honest AI Email Comparison 2026
summary: Notion Mail shut down on September 22, 2026. What to export, what stays in Gmail, and five replacements compared on price, AI drafting and labels.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Notion Mail shut down on September 22, 2026. Your email history is safe in Gmail, but drafts, scheduled emails, snippets and auto label instructions lived only in Notion Mail and had to be exported by September 21. The five realistic replacements are Slashy, Shortwave, Superhuman, Spark and Gmail with Gemini; which one fits depends on whether you want the AI to run the inbox or just tidy it.


If you opened Notion Mail this week and found a shutdown notice instead of your inbox, here is where things stand. Notion Mail always synced two ways with Gmail, so nothing you sent or received is gone. What is gone is the client: the views, the AI auto labels you wrote as prompts, the snippets and the scheduled sends. This page covers what happened, what you can still recover, and which replacement is worth your time.


## What happened to Notion Mail?


Notion announced the shutdown on June 25, 2026 and set the date for September 22. Notion's own explanation, reported by[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/25/notion-mail-shuts-down-amid-agent-takeover/) the same day, was that more than half of Notion Mail users were managing email without ever opening the inbox, and that the company was going all in on agents to run email instead of maintaining a client. Notion Mail had only been generally available since April 2025, built on the Skiff team Notion acquired in 2024.


Per[Notion's help center](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-mail-inbox-is-going-away-what-to-do-next) , September 21 was the last day to save anything, and unsaved data was deleted on the 22nd. Gmail AI connectors and mail blocks inside Notion pages keep working; only the inbox product is gone.


## What did I need to export, and what stays in Gmail?


Four things lived only in Notion Mail, per the same help page:


Item What Notion said to do Where it lands now


Drafts Migrate email drafts to Gmail Gmail Drafts, readable by any Gmail client


Scheduled emails Migrate scheduled emails to Gmail Gmail Scheduled, will still send on time


Snippets Export snippet content to use it elsewhere A file you paste into your next client


Auto label instructions Export auto label instructions to use elsewhere Prompts you rebuild as rules or labels


Everything else, meaning every message, label and thread, is already in Gmail because of the two-way sync. That is the good news: any replacement that connects to Gmail sees your full history on day one. The habit you lose is the Notion-style view of the inbox. No replacement below reproduces it exactly, and the honest advice is to pick the tool that solves the problem that made you try Notion Mail in the first place, which for most people was volume, not aesthetics.


## What is the best Notion Mail alternative?


Prices were read from each vendor's own pricing page in a browser on September 16, 2026, with monthly and annual billing listed separately.


Tool Email providers What it is Individual price Closest to Notion Mail on


**Slashy** Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365 AI-native client with memory, auto labels, snippets, calendar sidebar, iMessage and Slack control $30 monthly, or $25 billed annually AI labels that run themselves, snippets, scheduled send


**Shortwave** Gmail Gmail-native client built around AI search Free plan; Pro $18; Business $30, Premier $45, Max $120 per seat Snippets, AI filters, a clean Gmail-first design


**Superhuman** Gmail, Outlook Speed-focused client with AI on the Business tier Starter $30 monthly or $25 annually; Business $40 or $33 Custom auto labels (Business), snippets, split inbox


**Spark** Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Exchange, Yahoo, IMAP Cross-platform client with a free tier Free; Plus $10 monthly or $8.25 annually; Pro $20 or $16.58 Multi-provider unified inbox


**Gmail with Gemini** Gmail The default, with Gemini "Help me write" Included in Workspace, from $7 per user per month on annual Business Starter Nothing to migrate at all


Sources:[Slashy pricing](https://www.slashy.com/pricing) ,[Shortwave pricing](https://www.shortwave.com/pricing/) ,[Superhuman pricing](https://superhuman.com/pricing) ,[Spark pricing](https://sparkmailapp.com/pricing) ,[Google Workspace pricing](https://workspace.google.com/pricing) , all checked September 16, 2026.


An inbox that understands the next step


Slashy uses the context in your email and calendar to draft, schedule, remember, and follow through.


## Which alternative rebuilds Notion Mail's auto labels and snippets?


This is the feature most people miss, so it deserves its own answer.


Slashy triages every incoming message into labels automatically and lets you add your own in plain language, so a Notion Mail prompt like "flag anything from a candidate" becomes an automation rather than an instruction you re-run. Snippets and scheduled send are built in, and the same rules apply across every connected Gmail account. The AI drafts replies in your voice from a memory that learns continuously; on Slashy's own usage data, the share of drafts new users send without editing starts near 30% on day one and passes 80% by day 30.


> "The agent is unbelievable. The memory system actually works. It actually gets me."
>
>
> Suhail, Founder of Lunabill


Shortwave's pricing page lists AI filters (3 on Business, 10 on Premier, 50 on Max), auto-applied labels and snippets on paid tiers, with a Free plan that keeps basic intelligence and 90 days of AI search history. Superhuman puts custom auto labels, auto drafts and Ask AI on its Business tier at $40 monthly or $33 annually, and its[Mail AI page](https://superhuman.com/products/mail/ai) describes auto archiving of marketing and cold pitches. Spark's pricing page lists auto drafts and auto labels as coming soon rather than shipped, so it is the weakest match on this specific point. Gmail with Gemini has no prompt-based labels; you rebuild them as classic filters.


## Which alternative works with Outlook?


Notion Mail was Gmail only, so most readers of this page are on Gmail and every tool above applies. If your company is moving to Microsoft 365, the shortlist is Slashy (Gmail, Google Workspace, Outlook.com and Microsoft 365), Superhuman (a full client for Gmail and Outlook) and Spark (Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Exchange, Yahoo and IMAP). Shortwave is Gmail and Google Workspace only.


## What to choose if...


- **You liked that Notion Mail organized itself and want more of that:** Slashy, which labels, drafts and follows up from one memory on a single plan.
- **You want the closest thing to a free replacement:** Shortwave Free or Spark Free, or Gmail with Gemini if you already pay for Workspace.
- **You are on Outlook or a mixed provider setup:** Slashy, Superhuman or Spark.
- **You want the deepest AI search across years of Gmail:** Shortwave Premier or Max.
- **You keep your email in Notion pages via mail blocks and connectors:** those still work after the shutdown, so any Gmail client pairs with them.
- **You want to run email from iMessage, Slack or your own AI agent:** Slashy, which includes an MCP server and messaging control.
